AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If
 you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  APRIL 6, 2021

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale City Council meeting will be available to the public
electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  Roll Call – All Present
  a. Flag Salute: Mayor Agajanian
  b. Invocation: Aram Adjemian, City Clerk

  Regular Meeting of the Glendale City Council was Posted on March 30, 2021 on

3. PRESENTATIONS AND APPOINTMENTS
  a. Agenda Preview for the Meetings of Tuesday, April 13, 2021
  Meetings cancelled on April 13. The next regular meetings will be on April 20, 2021.

  b. Senator Anthony Portantino’s Legislative Update

  Staff Comment:
  Police Chief Carl Povilaitis

  c. CERT Program Overview and Future
  Fire Captain Jonathan Payne

  d. Outgoing Mayor’s Comments
  Mayor Agajanian stated he was the only mayor to serve an entire year during a
  worldwide pandemic and unfortunately had not experienced events and trips compared
  to previous mayors. However, the public had access to his phone numbers and studio
  office and received thousands of calls and hundreds of visits asking for help regarding
  housing, traffic, landlord-tenant building issues, etc. One of his main objectives was to
  act as a leader, mediator, and coordinator, not as an oracle; and to give chances to
  Council Members to voice their opinion. He wanted to avoid wasting time by repeating
  issues and statements already expressed by his colleagues and only gave his input
  when it was different from what was stated already. 2020 was an extraordinary year and
  found that what makes a great city is the community and how much we supported one
  another. The city remained strong while it navigated through unchartered territory during
  the pandemic. He made sure to prioritize the health and safety of the community and

  04 06 21
  CC
  4A
   helped implement relief programs (rental assistance, affordable housing units, financial
  rent subsidy for qualified applicants, small business grant programs, distributed gallons
  of sanitizers, approval of al fresco dining program, slow streets program, ban Mylar
  balloons, ban flavored tobacco, and established sustainability commission). He thanked
  the Glendale Police Dept. and Fire Dept. for ensuring the safety of the community. He
  recognized the community partnership with healthcare facilities in providing COVID-19
  testing and vaccination sites; and recently, administering vaccines to homebound
  seniors. Lastly, he thanked everyone for making his year as Mayor a successful one
  even during an unforeseen pandemic and looked forward to serving the community
  alongside his colleagues and the employees of the City of Glendale.

e. Selection of a New Mayor
  City Clerk Aram Adjemian entertained nominations for the Office of the Mayor. Council
  Member Brotman nominated Council Member Devine for Mayor. Council Member
  Kassakhian seconded. Hearing no further nominations, Mr. Adjemian proceeded with the
  Roll Call.
  Vote as Follows
  Ayes:  Brotman, Devine, Kassakhian, Najarian, Agajanian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  City Clerk Aram Adjemian declared Council Member Devine the duly elected Mayor of
  the City of Glendale.

f. New Mayor’s Comments
  Newly appointed Mayor Devine thanked his colleagues and the community for entrusting
  her with this position. The shared goals to make the neighborhood stronger, safer, and
  healthier are still at the core of who they are and the reason for everything that they do
  and in every decision that Council makes together. She commended former Mayor
  Agajanian for his fine service during this difficult year and for his continuous pursuit of
  more affordable housing. Her goals for this year: cleaner and greener Grayson
  Repowering Plant for 100% renewable energy; join the Worldwide Coalition of Mayor
  advocating for climate change mitigation; continue to support our business community to
  recover from the pandemic; launch tech incubator program; access to a faster more
  reliable transportation with the bus rapid transit; support upgrading the infrastructure;
  advocating for more parks green space; affordable housing; protection of historic
  resources; promote and support anti-racism; setting up the blue ribbon panel for Pension
  Reform; and the groundbreaking of the Armenian American Museum and Cultural
  Center. Finally, she is committed to listening to all of the residents’ voices, promises to
  stand up for the community, and is humbled and honored to serve for the next year as
  Mayor.
